questions.question_text: In which part of the brain are mammillary bodies located?
questions.explanation: Mammillary bodies are located in the hypothalamus.

questions.question_text: Where do the anterior thalamic nuclei receive their afferents from?
questions.explanation: The anterior thalamic nuclei receive their afferents from the mammillary body.

questions.question_text: A 39-year-old man has partial optic nerve damage. Which visual field defect is most likely to occur?
questions.explanation: Partial optic nerve damage typically results in an ipsilateral scotoma.

questions.question_text: A 45-year-old woman developed homonymous upper quadrantanopia. Where is the lesion most likely to be located in the visual pathway?
questions.explanation: Homonymous upper quadrantanopia is often associated with a lesion in Meyer’s loop.

questions.question_text: In which part of the frontal lobe is Broca’s area situated?
questions.explanation: Broca’s area is located in the frontal operculum.

questions.question_text: Where does the hypothalamus originate from?
questions.explanation: The hypothalamus originates from the diencephalon.

questions.question_text: Which of the following consists of the basal forebrain?
questions.explanation: The basal forebrain includes structures like the nucleus basalis of Meynert.

questions.question_text: Which of the following cranial nerve fibres terminates in the anterior and posterior cochlear nuclei?
questions.explanation: The vestibulocochlear nerve (cranial nerve VIII) terminates in the cochlear nuclei.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a part of the cortical area of the limbic lobe?
questions.explanation: The cingulate gyrus is part of the cortical area of the limbic lobe.

questions.question_text: A 54-year-old woman presents with multiple intracranial and spinal tumours, mainly schwannomas and neurofibromas. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: The presentation is consistent with bilateral acoustic neurofibromatosis (NF2).

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a characteristic feature of frontotemporal dementia?
questions.explanation: Pick’s bodies are characteristic histopathological features of frontotemporal dementia.

questions.question_text: Which of the following are the characteristic macroscopic changes seen in multi-infarct dementia?
questions.explanation: Multi-infarct dementia is associated with arteriosclerotic changes in major arteries.

questions.question_text: Which of the following are the characteristic histopathological changes seen in Lewy body dementia?
questions.explanation: Neuritic plaques are characteristic of Lewy body dementia.

questions.question_text: Which of the following tumours are embryonal in origin?
questions.explanation: Medulloblastomas are embryonal tumours.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a characteristic feature of Prion disease?

options.text: Amyloid plaques containing PrP and b-amyloid protein
Gliosis which is rarely seen in prion disease

questions.explanation: Prion diseases are characterized by amyloid plaques containing prion protein (PrP).

questions.question_text: Secretion of which of the following hormones is inhibited by dopamine?
questions.explanation: Dopamine inhibits the secretion of prolactin.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is an inhibitory hypothalamic hormone?
questions.explanation: Somatostatin is an inhibitory hormone produced in the hypothalamus.

questions.question_text: Which of the following receptors is linked with a moderate (10–100 m/s) second messenger?
questions.explanation: Receptors linked with moderate speed second messengers include m-receptors.

questions.question_text: Which group of nerve fibres innervates tendon organs?
questions.explanation: Ib fibres innervate tendon organs (Golgi tendon organs).

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about neuronal action potential is correct?

options.text: Action potential is conducted along axons with decrement
Closing of potassium channels is associated with repolarisation
Conduction is independent of the resistance and conductance of the membrane
During the action potential the neuronal membrane can be stimulated
Influx of sodium into the cell leads to depolarisation

correct_answer.text: Influx of sodium into the cell leads to depolarisation

correct_answers.text: Influx of sodium into the cell leads to depolarisation

questions.explanation: The influx of sodium ions into the cell is responsible for depolarisation during an action potential.

questions.question_text: Which of the neurohormones stimulates growth hormone release?
questions.explanation: A neurohormone is a chemical that is released by neuroendocrine cells of the hypothalamus and   acts at a specific distant site or sites. β-Endorphin and cortisol are not neurohormones. β-Endorphin   is an endogenous opioid peptide neurotransmitter. Cortisol is a steroid hormone secreted by the   adrenal gland.  It stimulates hormone secretion as follows:

questions.question_text: Which of the following is the precursor in the synthesis of acetylcholine?
questions.explanation: Choline is the precursor for the synthesis of acetylcholine.

questions.question_text: Which of the following best describes g-aminobutyric acid A receptors?
questions.explanation: GABA-A receptors are ligand-gated ion channels.

questions.question_text: What changes have been reported on pre- and postmortem studies of patients with depression?

options.text: Decreased muscarinic receptors in limbic area
Increased nicotinic receptors in cortical area

questions.explanation: Studies have shown decreased 5-HT2 receptors in the limbic areas of individuals with depression.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a precursor in the synthesis of dopamine?
questions.explanation: l-Tyrosine is the primary precursor in the synthesis of dopamine.

questions.question_text: Which of the following neurotransmitters was discovered first?
questions.explanation: Biogenic amines are well understood and were the first of the neurotransmitters to be discovered.

questions.question_text: A 70-year-old man was diagnosed with vascular dementia. Which of the following diagnostic systems does not require neuroimaging for vascular dementia?

options.text: Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, 4th edn (DSM-IV)
The ICD-10 (International Classification of Diseases, 10th revision)

questions.explanation: Hachinski’s scale can be used for diagnosing vascular dementia without the need for neuroimaging.

questions.question_text: In which year was computed tomography made available for clinical practice?
questions.explanation: Computed tomography (CT) was first made available for clinical practice in 1972.

questions.question_text: Single photon emission computed tomography study in Alzheimer’s disease has shown reduced regional blood flow. Which part of the brain is implicated in this?
questions.explanation: Reduced regional blood flow in Alzheimer’s disease is commonly seen in the prefrontal area.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about Huntington’s disease is correct?

options.text: Dopamine concentration is increased in striatum
Extrapyramidal neuronal loss occurs in frontal cortex
g-Aminobutyric acid concentration is decreased in caudate nucleus
It mainly affects the frontal and temporal lobes

correct_answer.text: g-Aminobutyric acid concentration is decreased in caudate nucleus

correct_answers.text: g-Aminobutyric acid concentration is decreased in caudate nucleus

questions.explanation: In Huntington's disease, there is a decrease in g-Aminobutyric acid (GABA) concentration in the caudate nucleus.

questions.question_text: Which of the statements about the elimination of clonidine is correct?

options.text: Clonidine is completely excreted by kidneys unchanged
Clonidine is metabolised completely in the liver before its excretion
Plasma half-life of clonidine is 24 hours
Rate of clonidine metabolism increases with age
Rate of clonidine metabolism is highest in young children under the age of 6

correct_answer.text: Rate of clonidine metabolism is highest in young children under the age of 6

correct_answers.text: Rate of clonidine metabolism is highest in young children under the age of 6

questions.explanation: Clonidine is primarily metabolised in the liver before being excreted.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is consistent with the concept of neurotransmitters?

options.text: They are released from the presynaptic terminal when the neuron repolarises
They bind to a receptor, and cause an effect in postsynaptic neurons
The reuptake mechanism can be presynaptic or postsynaptic
They are stored actively in the presynaptic terminal
They are synthesised by presynaptic and postsynaptic neurons

correct_answer.text: They bind to a receptor, and cause an effect in postsynaptic neurons

correct_answers.text: They bind to a receptor, and cause an effect in postsynaptic neurons

questions.explanation: Neurotransmitters bind to receptors on postsynaptic neurons to exert their effects.

questions.question_text: What is the rate-limiting step in the synthesis of dopamine?
questions.explanation: Tyrosine hydroxylase is the rate-limiting enzyme in the synthesis of dopamine.

questions.question_text: A patient receives an injection of flupenthixol decanoate 50 mg intramuscularly every 2 weeks. In terms of its absorption, what order of kinetics does flupenthixol decanoate follow?
questions.explanation: Flupenthixol decanoate follows zero-order kinetics due to its long half-life.

questions.question_text: Which of the following drugs leads to sensitisation?
questions.explanation: Amphetamines are known to cause sensitisation, leading to increased response with repeated use.

questions.question_text: Which of the following results in increased excretion of lithium?
questions.explanation: Acetazolamide can increase the renal excretion of lithium.

questions.question_text: Which of the following pharmacological profiles belongs to bifeprunox?

options.text: Binds to D2-, (5-HT2A-), 5-HT2C-, a1-/a2-, low affinity for H1- and muscarinic receptors
Blocks D1-, D2- and D4-receptors and a1-/a2-receptors; postural hypotension and hyperprolactinemia are common
D1- and D4-receptor antagonist, 5-HT2A-receptor agonist, strong antihistaminic side effects
D2-/5-HT2A-receptor antagonist, little activity at H1- and muscarinic receptors, insomnia is a common adverse effect
D2-receptor partial agonist, 5-HT1A-receptor agonist, low potential for weight gain, extrapyramidal symptoms and hyperprolactinemia

correct_answer.text: D2-receptor partial agonist, 5-HT1A-receptor agonist, low potential for weight gain, extrapyramidal symptoms and hyperprolactinemia

correct_answers.text: D2-receptor partial agonist, 5-HT1A-receptor agonist, low potential for weight gain, extrapyramidal symptoms and hyperprolactinemia

questions.explanation: Bifeprunox is a D2-receptor partial agonist and a 5-HT1A-receptor agonist.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is the most appropriate strategy for switching from mirtazapine to venlafaxine?

options.text: Withdraw mirtazapine and then start venlafaxine
Withdraw mirtazapine and wait for 2 weeks before starting venlafaxine
Withdraw mirtazapine and wait for 24–48 hours before starting venlafaxine
Withdraw mirtazapine and wait for a week before starting venlafaxine

questions.explanation: Cross-tapering is recommended to minimize withdrawal symptoms and manage side effects.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a contraindication for sildenafil?
questions.explanation: Myocardial infarction is a contraindication for the use of sildenafil due to potential cardiovascular risks.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about differences in the drugs used for dementia is correct?

options.text: Galantamine decreases the sensitivity of acetylcholine receptors, whereas donepezil and rivastigmine do not
Half-lives of donepezil and rivastigmine are about 40 hours and 12 hours respectively
Memantine works by protecting neurons from excessive stimulation
Rivastigmine and galantamine have less peripheral activity outside the central nervous system than donepezil
Rivastigmine is highly protein bound whereas donepezil circulates mostly unbound

correct_answer.text: Memantine works by protecting neurons from excessive stimulation

correct_answers.text: Memantine works by protecting neurons from excessive stimulation

questions.explanation: Memantine works by blocking NMDA receptors and protects neurons from excessive stimulation.

questions.question_text: A 20-year-old man presented with trigeminal neuralgia in the pain clinic. He was prescribed carbamazepine. Which of the following receptors mediate the nociceptic action of carbamazepine?
questions.explanation: Carbamazepine exerts its analgesic effect primarily through GABA-A receptor modulation.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a mechanism of action of galantamine?

options.text: It acts as a N-methyl-d-aspartate (NMDA) receptor antagonist
It is an irreversible inhibitor of anticholinesterase
It is a nicotine acetylcholine receptor antagonist
It is a NMDA receptor agonist
It is a reversible inhibitor of anticholinesterase

correct_answer.text: It is a reversible inhibitor of anticholinesterase

correct_answers.text: It is a reversible inhibitor of anticholinesterase

questions.explanation: Galantamine is a reversible inhibitor of acetylcholinesterase.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a mechanism of action of aripiprazole?
questions.explanation: Aripiprazole acts as a partial agonist at D2 receptors.

questions.question_text: A 70-year-old woman taking an antidepressant for the last 3 weeks was admitted to a medical ward following a seizure. This was associated with a history of nausea, dizziness, lethargy, confusion and cramps. Which of the following drugs has been reported the least as being responsible for this presentation?
questions.explanation: Fluoxetine has been reported the least among the listed drugs for causing seizures.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is most likely to develop earlier in the course of serotonin syndrome rather than late?
questions.explanation: Hyperreflexia is an early symptom of serotonin syndrome.

questions.question_text: A 34-year-old woman on lithium for about 5 years presented to her general practitioner with adverse effects. Which of the following is suggestive of lithium toxicity?
questions.explanation: Nausea and vomiting are common signs of lithium toxicity.

questions.question_text: What is the mechanism of sedation caused by clonidine?
questions.explanation: Nausea and vomiting are common signs of lithium toxicity.

questions.question_text: Which of the following drugs causes hyperprolactinemia?
questions.explanation: Fluoxetine and other SSRIs can cause hyperprolactinemia due to their effects on serotonin.

questions.question_text: Which of the following can result in postinjection delirium/sedation syndrome?
questions.explanation: Postinjection delirium/sedation syndrome is associated with olanzapine pamoate.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a dose-related side effect?
questions.explanation: Clozapine-related seizures are dose-dependent and increase with higher doses.

questions.question_text: Which of the following side effects of antipsychotics is not dose dependent?
questions.explanation: Neuroleptic malignant syndrome can occur independently of dose.

questions.question_text: A 23-year-old man with schizophrenia was treated with antipsychotic medication. He complained of breast discharge and loss of libido. Which of the following antipsychotics should be used as an alternative option?
questions.explanation: Amisulpride has a lower risk of hyperprolactinemia compared to the other options.

questions.question_text: Which of the following drugs is least effective as a prophylactic agent for bipolar affective disorder?
questions.explanation: Clozapine is not typically used as a prophylactic agent for bipolar disorder.

questions.question_text: What is the fortnightly maintenance dose of olanzapine pamoate injection after 2 months of treatment for a patient taking 15 mg olanzapine?
questions.explanation: For adult patients taking oral olanzapine 10 mg daily, the initiation would be with 210 mg every   2 weeks or 405 mg every 4 weeks, then a maintenance dose after 2 months’ treatment would be   150 mg every 2 weeks or 300 mg every 4 weeks.  For patients taking oral olanzapine 15 mg daily, the initial dose would be 300 mg every 2 weeks   and then a maintenance dose after 2 months’ treatment could be 210 mg every 2 weeks or 405 mg   every 4 weeks.  For patients taking oral olanzapine 20 mg daily, the initial dose would be 300 mg every 2 weeks,   then a maintenance dose after 2 months’ treatment of 300 mg every 2 weeks. The dose could be   adjusted according to the response. The maximum dose is 300 mg every 2 weeks

questions.question_text: A 55-year-old man was referred by the cardiologist for assessment of his depression. He has had a myocardial infarction (MI) recently. Which antidepressant has the best evidence base for its use in post-MI depression?
questions.explanation: Sertraline has the best evidence for safety and efficacy in patients with a history of MI.

questions.question_text: A 30-year-old man diagnosed with schizophrenia was treated with three different antipsychotics for about 6 months at therapeutic doses without any significant improvement. He was started on clozapine recently. What are the chances that his condition will respond to clozapine?
questions.explanation: Clozapine has a response rate of approximately 30-50% in treatment-resistant schizophrenia.

questions.question_text: A drug causes release of catecholamines as well as serotonin. This drug is taken up in serotoninergic neurons by the serotonin transporter responsible for 5-hydroxytryptamine (5-HT) reuptake and, once inside the neuron, it causes rapid release of a bolus of 5-HT. What is this drug called?
questions.explanation: Ecstasy (MDMA) causes the release of both catecholamines and serotonin.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statement applies to varenicline?

options.text: It is indicated for the treatment of opioid dependence
It is recommended to be used for 6 weeks in one course of treatment
It is a D2-receptor partial agonist
Its use can precipitate or exacerbate psychosis

correct_answer.text: It is indicated for the treatment of opioid dependence

correct_answers.text: It is indicated for the treatment of opioid dependence

questions.explanation: Varenicline can precipitate or exacerbate psychosis, particularly in individuals with a history of psychosis.

questions.question_text: Which of the following will demonstrate fragile sites in chromosomes?

options.text: Culturing cells in conditions devoid of thymidine
Culturing cells in medium devoid of folate
Culturing cells in medium devoid of vitamin B12

correct_answer.text: Culturing cells in conditions devoid of thymidine

correct_answers.text: Culturing cells in conditions devoid of thymidine

questions.explanation: Culturing cells in conditions devoid of thymidine can reveal fragile sites in chromosomes.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about the structure of DNA is correct?

options.text: Its backbone is made of two chains of sugars wrapped in the form of double helix, held together by hydrogen bonds
Its backbone is made from alternating phosphate and sugar residues, held together by hydrogen bonds
It has two chains of nucleotides wrapped in the form of a double helix, held together by ester bonds
It has two chains of nucleotides wrapped in the form of a double helix, held together by hydrogen bonds
It has two chains of nucleotides wrapped in the form of a double helix, held together by covalent bonds

correct_answer.text: It has two chains of nucleotides wrapped in the form of a double helix, held together by hydrogen bonds

correct_answers.text: It has two chains of nucleotides wrapped in the form of a double helix, held together by hydrogen bonds

questions.explanation: The structure of DNA consists of two chains of nucleotides wrapped in a double helix, held together by hydrogen bonds.

questions.question_text: Of what is the basic repeat unit of DNA made?

options.text: Deoxyribose sugar, a carbon group and a nitrogenous base
Deoxyribose sugar and a nitrogenous base
Deoxyribose sugar and a phosphate group
Deoxyribose sugar, nitrogenous base and a carbon group
Deoxyribose sugar, nitrogenous base and a phosphate group

correct_answer.text: Deoxyribose sugar, nitrogenous base and a phosphate group

correct_answers.text: Deoxyribose sugar, nitrogenous base and a phosphate group

questions.explanation: The basic repeat unit of DNA is made up of deoxyribose sugar, a nitrogenous base, and a phosphate group.

questions.question_text: Which of the following cell organelles is essential for translation or decoding?
questions.explanation: Ribosomes are the cellular organelles responsible for protein synthesis or translation.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about mitosis is correct?

options.text: It contains only one of each pair of chromosomes
It means segregation of parent cells

questions.explanation: Mitosis results in two identical daughter cells, maintaining the diploid chromosome number.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about the frame-shift mutation responsible for Tay–Sachs disease is correct?

options.text: There is breakage of a fragment of chromosome and re-joining at a different site
A piece of DNA is gained
There is a simple change in one base of the gene sequence due to substitution of one base by another
There is a loss of one base, causing the triplet code to be read out of the frame
There is a loss in the sequence of bases

correct_answer.text: There is a loss of one base, causing the triplet code to be read out of the frame

correct_answers.text: There is a loss of one base, causing the triplet code to be read out of the frame

questions.explanation: A frame-shift mutation involves the loss of a base, altering the reading frame of the gene.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about restriction enzymes found mainly in bacteria is correct?

options.text: They act by cutting DNA randomly
They are also called restriction methyltransferases
They are mainly used for modification of RNA in the laboratory settings
They can be used to get fragments of easily manageable base-pair sizes (10^3–10^4), thus allowing genes to be handled almost in isolation
They are used by bacteria for the synthesis of bacterial protein

correct_answer.text: They can be used to get fragments of easily manageable base-pair sizes (10^3–10^4), thus allowing genes to be handled almost in isolation

correct_answers.text: They can be used to get fragments of easily manageable base-pair sizes (10^3–10^4), thus allowing genes to be handled almost in isolation

questions.explanation: Restriction enzymes cut DNA at specific sites, allowing for manageable fragment sizes.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about reverse transcriptase is correct?

options.text: It is used in synthesis of complementary DNA from mRNA
It is used to break down tRNA into different segments
It is used to stop the synthesis of a defective protein in humans
It is used for modification of RNA in laboratory settings

correct_answer.text: It is used in synthesis of complementary DNA from mRNA

correct_answers.text: It is used in synthesis of complementary DNA from mRNA

questions.explanation: Reverse transcriptase synthesizes complementary DNA (cDNA) from mRNA.

questions.question_text: Denaturing gradient gel electrophoresis, chemical cleavage, single-strand conformational analysis and heteroduplex analysis are used for identification of causal mutations. What is the basis of this process?
questions.explanation: These techniques are based on DNA sequencing for identifying causal mutations.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about restriction fragment length polymorphism analysis is correct?

options.text: It is detected by south-western blotting
It is generally inherited in a non-mendelian fashion
It is an important component of positional cloning
It is based on the fact that DNA fragments produced by digestion by a certain restriction enzyme will be of different lengths in different individuals
It is based on the fact that DNA fragments produced by digestion by a certain restriction enzyme will be same lengths in different individuals because they cleave at a specific base sequence site

correct_answer.text: It is based on the fact that DNA fragments produced by digestion by a certain restriction enzyme will be of different lengths in different individuals

correct_answers.text: It is based on the fact that DNA fragments produced by digestion by a certain restriction enzyme will be of different lengths in different individuals

questions.explanation: Restriction fragment length polymorphism (RFLP) analysis is based on DNA fragment length variations.

questions.question_text: To what does genetics imprinting lead?

options.text: Change in the sequence of DNA

questions.explanation: Genetic imprinting leads to irreversible gene inactivation, depending on the parental origin.

questions.question_text: Which are the commonest association studies in psychiatric literature?
questions.explanation: Candidate gene association studies are commonly used in psychiatric genetics research.

questions.question_text: What is the heritability of antisocial behaviour?
questions.explanation: The heritability of antisocial behavior is estimated to be around 40%.

questions.question_text: To date, which condition has the strongest evidence for gene and environment interaction?
questions.explanation: Schizophrenia shows strong evidence for gene-environment interactions.

questions.question_text: Which of the following metabolic diseases has X-linked transmission?
questions.explanation: Hunter's syndrome is an X-linked recessive disorder.

questions.question_text: When we consider linkage studies with heterogeneity, what does ‘allelic heterogeneity’ mean?

options.text: The cases are either polygenic in inheritance or not genetic at all
Two or more loci at which an allelic mutation occurs result in different phenotypes
Two or more mutant alleles existing at different loci result in same phenotypes
Two or more mutant alleles existing at same locus result in same phenotypes
Two or more mutant alleles existing at same locus result in different phenotypes

correct_answer.text: Two or more mutant alleles existing at same locus result in different phenotypes

correct_answers.text: Two or more mutant alleles existing at same locus result in different phenotypes

questions.explanation: Allelic heterogeneity refers to different mutations within the same gene causing similar phenotypes.

questions.question_text: What does the term ‘vertical inheritance’ in genetics mean?

options.text: Transmission of disease from mother to offspring
Transmission of disease from father to offspring
The phenomenon that affected individuals is found in every generation
The phenomenon that affected individuals is seen every second generation
No cases may occur in a previous generation, and the disease may manifest in children of the next generation

correct_answer.text: The phenomenon that affected individuals is found in every generation

correct_answers.text: The phenomenon that affected individuals is found in every generation

questions.explanation: Vertical inheritance indicates that the trait is consistently passed from one generation to the next.

questions.question_text: In neurofibromatosis, some patients may have only café-au-lait spots, whereas others may have more features including neurofibromas, café-au-lait spots. What is the phenomenon called in which there is manifestation of symptoms of variable degree in different individuals with the same genotype?
questions.explanation: Expressivity refers to the varying degrees of expression of a genetic trait.

questions.question_text: Which of the RNA polymerases is involved in protein synthesis in humans?
questions.explanation: RNA polymerase II is responsible for synthesizing mRNA, which is translated into proteins.

questions.question_text: Which of the following disturbs the Hardy–Weinberg equilibrium?

options.text: A population that does not allow migrated communities to mix with them
Marriages among close relatives not allowed
No changes in gene frequencies because of a chance factor
Mating among professionals with a high IQ

correct_answer.text: Mating among professionals with a high IQ

correct_answers.text: Mating among professionals with a high IQ

questions.explanation: Restricted mixing of populations disturbs the Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is an endophenotype related to sensory gating deficits in schizophrenia?
questions.explanation: Prepulse inhibition is an endophenotype associated with sensory gating deficits in schizophrenia.

questions.question_text: Which of the following genes is implicated in the transport of amyloid precursor protein to endoplasmic reticulum for degradation?
questions.explanation: The SORL1 gene is involved in the trafficking of amyloid precursor protein.

questions.question_text: What is the concordance rate of schizophrenia in dizygotic twins?
questions.explanation: The concordance rate of schizophrenia in dizygotic twins is about 30%.

questions.question_text: Smoking cannabis at young age increases the risk of developing schizophrenia. Which of the concepts explains this association?
questions.explanation: Epigenetics explains how environmental factors like cannabis use can interact with genetic predisposition.

questions.question_text: What is the prevalence of 22Q deletion syndrome in patients with schizophrenia?
questions.explanation: 22Q deletion syndrome has a prevalence of about 5% in individuals with schizophrenia.

questions.question_text: A 45-year-old man with choreiform movements presented in the neuropsychiatric clinic. He was diagnosed with Huntington’s disease. Genetic testing showed that he had the Huntingtin gene in only one of the chromosomes (C4). His wife did not have Huntington’s disease. He wanted to know the chances of his son developing the disorder. What would you say to him?
questions.explanation: There is a 50% chance of inheriting the Huntingtin gene from an affected parent.

questions.question_text: Which of the following describes path analysis correctly?

options.text: Analyse the path of a patient through the services
Analysis of biochemical pathways in the brain of mentally disordered individuals
Analysis of evolution of symptoms in a mentally disordered individual
Analysis of the gene–environment interaction using biological techniques
Analysis of the gene–environment interaction using statistical techniques

correct_answer.text: Analysis of the gene–environment interaction using statistical techniques

correct_answers.text: Analysis of the gene–environment interaction using statistical techniques

questions.explanation: Path analysis is a statistical technique used to describe the directed dependencies among a set of variables.

questions.question_text: What is the unit of measurement of genetic distance?
questions.explanation: Genetic distance is measured in centimorgans, which reflect the likelihood of recombination between genes.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is the most accurate definition of a recombination fraction?

options.text: It is defined as the fraction of genes that cross-over
It is defined as the number of recombinants divided by the total number of offsprings
It is defined as the total number of offspring divided by the number of recombinants
It is defined as the total number of recombinants divided by the number of recombinants
It is defined as the total number of recombinants divided by the total number of offspring

correct_answer.text: It is defined as the number of recombinants divided by the total number of offsprings

correct_answers.text: It is defined as the number of recombinants divided by the total number of offsprings

questions.explanation: The recombination fraction is defined as the number of recombinants divided by the total number of offspring.

questions.question_text: You analysed the genome of a person to find the genetic marker for Huntington's disease. For him to be negative for the genetic marker, what should the logarithm of odds score be?
questions.explanation: Logarithm of odds (LOD) score was described by Newton E Mortonin in 1955. The LOD score is a statistical test that helps to calculate linkage distances. It is a technique used in human, plant and animal linkage studies. The presence of linkage is suggested by a +LOD score whereas the chances of linkage are likely to be less if –LOD scores are found.

questions.question_text: What is the genotypic correlation between two siblings?
questions.explanation: Genotypic correlation between dizygotic twins as well as siblings is 0.5, i.e. they have 50% genes in common. Genotypic correlation for monozygotic twins is 1. They have 100% genes common to both.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about schizotaxia is correct?

options.text: It is ataxia in a patient with schizophrenia
It is a form of thought disorder seen in patients with schizophrenia
It is a form of thought disorder seen in schizotypal personality disorder
It is a liability to develop schizophrenia from childhood

correct_answer.text: It is a liability to develop schizophrenia from childhood

correct_answers.text: It is a liability to develop schizophrenia from childhood

questions.explanation: Originally Paul Meehl used the word schizotaxia to describe the liability to develop schizophrenia or a schizophrenia-like conditions. Gene–environment interactions lead to development of schizophrenia or schizophrenia-like disorders in susceptible individuals. This susceptibility is expressed through a combination of cognitive, neurobiological and social skills deficits in childhood and this is called schizotaxia.

questions.question_text: What type of study would you consider if you want to understand why some people cope with a chronic illness well, whereas others find it difficult to cope?
questions.explanation: Qualitative research is also known as interpretive research. It tries to study things in their natural setting, attempting to make sense of, or interpret, phenomena in terms of the meanings that people bring to them. The data are usually gathered with semi-structured individual interviews, in focus group sessions or by simple observations. Such observations may not be generalised to wider populations, but may generate a hypothesis for further testing.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about a confounder is correct?

options.text: It is a variable that is present on the casual pathway between the exposure and the outcome
It cannot be reduced by restricting the study population
It varies systematically with an exposure and acts as an independent risk or protective factor for the disease
It is a variable introduced to minimise the biases in the study
It should not be in a triangular relationship with the other variables

correct_answer.text: It varies systematically with an exposure and acts as an independent risk or protective factor for the disease

correct_answers.text: It varies systematically with an exposure and acts as an independent risk or protective factor for the disease

questions.explanation: A confounder is a variable that is associated with both exposure and outcome, but not on the causal pathway. Restricting the study population sample can reduce the influence of the confounders. Age and sex are the common confounders.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is the most common psychiatric disorder in primary care?
questions.explanation: The frequency of neurotic condition in descending order is mixed anxiety and depression 48%, GAD 28%, depression14%, phobias 12%, OCD 10% and panic disorder 6%.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is associated with twice the risk of developing a neurotic disorder amongst the general population?

options.text: Belonging to a lower social class

questions.explanation: The incidence of developing neurotic illness increases with increasing environmental stress. All the above factors are associated with the development of neurotic disorder. The risk is twice for prisoners and homeless.

questions.question_text: How common are specific phobias in the general population?
questions.explanation: About 10% of the general population have specific phobias. The lifetime prevalence is 11.3%. The 12-month national co-morbidity survey (NCS) prevalence is 8.8% and the 6-month epidemiological catchment area study (ECA) prevalence is 4.5–11.9%. In the DSM- IV, there are five types of specific phobias mentioned: 1. animals 2. aspects of the natural environment 3. blood, injection and injury 4. situations 5. other provoking agents. Animal and social phobias are more common in females.

questions.question_text: An audit of suicides in 5000 depressed patients in a population found that 100 patients had taken their own life. The rate of suicide therefore was 100/5000. What does this rate refer to?
questions.explanation: This refers to the ratio of the number of deaths due to a particular disease, e.g. depression, in a given population and those in the total population. The crude mortality rate is the ratio of deaths due to all causes in a given population and those in the total population. The case fatality rate refers to comparison of the number of deaths in patients with a given diagnosis with the total number of patients with the same diagnosis. The proportional mortality rate refers to the comparison of number of deaths in patients with a condition with deaths due to all causes in the population.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about variant Creutzfeldt–Jakob disease (vCJD) is correct when compared with CJD?

options.text: EEG abnormalities are less common in variant CJD
The 'pulvinar sign' on MRI is not a diagnostic sign in variant CJD
Variant CJD has a delayed onset
Variant CJD has a rapid course
Variant CJD rarely presents with psychiatric features such as depression and personality changes

correct_answer.text: EEG abnormalities are less common in variant CJD

correct_answers.text: EEG abnormalities are less common in variant CJD

questions.explanation: Variant Creutzfeldt–Jakob disease (vCJD) has an earlier onset. It has a slower course. The 'pulvinar sign' on MRI is a useful diagnostic sign in vCJD. The vCJD usually presents with psychiatric symptoms including depression and personality changes. Bovine spongiform encephalopathy (BSE) and vCJD are caused by the same prion strain and there is no doubt that vCJD occurs on eating contaminated beef products. Usually there is a polymorphism at codon 129 of the prion protein (PrP) gene encoding for either methionine or valine, whereas almost all patients with vCJD are homozygous at codon 129 of the PrP gene that encodes for methionine. Electroencephalography abnormalities are less common in vCJD.

questions.question_text: What is the percentage of the transvestites who are diagnosed as having a personality disorder?
questions.explanation: Transvestism is sometimes seen among obsessive personalities. Some studies suggest that around 50–70% of transvestites can be diagnosed as having a personality disorder.

questions.question_text: In which age group does three-quarters of life-time mental illness occur?
questions.explanation: It has been suggested that about 50% of all mental illness arises by the age of 14 years and about 75% of all lifetime illnesses by the mid-20s. When measured in 2004, nearly a quarter of the burden of disease in the UK was due to mental health disorder, and this was higher than cardiovascular diseases or cancer.

questions.question_text: Evidence suggested that the rate of suicide had increased manyfold in women who were imprisoned. What is the likely increase?
questions.explanation: Studies have shown that suicide is a major public health issue and a significant cause of death. Rates of suicide and self-harm are higher in certain age groups compared with others. When compared with a normal population, people with severe mental health disorders have a 20-fold higher rate of suicide. The rate is even higher (30-fold) in those who have history of self-harm. In prisoners the rates of suicide are higher in women (20 times) compared with men (5 times). Other groups that are at a higher risk of suicide are young men and those from black and ethnic minority groups. There has been a significant rise in self-harm by young people in the last decade.

questions.question_text: What percentage of people with mental illness consume tobacco in the UK?
questions.explanation: Smoking is a preventable illness. On an average the lifespan of a smoker is 10 years less than that of a non-smoker. The prevalence of smoking in the general population is 21%. The prevalence of smoking is highest in those who have a mental illness and are in prison (80%), or attend methadone maintenance clinics (80%). The rate of smoking is around 70% in those who are inpatients on mental health wards. Roughly half of all tobacco consumed in the UK is by those who have mental illness.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about head injury is correct?

options.text: Children are at greater risk from 5–15 years of age
On average 1000/100,0000 attend hospital with a head injury every year
Only 50% of the head injuries are severe
Risk factors include higher socioeconomic class
Road traffic accidents are the commonest cause of head injury

correct_answer.text: Road traffic accidents are the commonest cause of head injury

correct_answers.text: Road traffic accidents are the commonest cause of head injury

questions.explanation: Around 200–300/100,000 people attend hospitals every year for head injury. About one-sixth of them will need admission. About 80% of head injuries are mild, 10% moderate and 10% severe. Road traffic accidents are by far the largest cause of head injuries, followed by assaults and falls. A significant number of people also get head injury due to deliberate self-harm. Alcohol misuse and lower socioeconomic status are high risk factors. Around 100/100,000 people have considerable disability due to head injury.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about the association of immigration with schizophrenia is correct?

options.text: Risk is higher in second-generation migrants than first-generation migrants
Risk is higher for first-generation migrants than second-generation migrants
Risk is higher for migrants from higher socioeconomic status
Risk is higher for white people moving into black societies
Risk is increased in the parents but not the siblings of the second generation

correct_answer.text: Risk is higher for first-generation migrants than second-generation migrants

correct_answers.text: Risk is higher for first-generation migrants than second-generation migrants

questions.explanation: Relative risk for first-generation migrants is 2.7 compared with 4.5 in the second-generation migrants. Risk is higher for migrants from a lower socioeconomic status and in black people moving to dominantly white countries. Also, there is a greater risk in siblings rather than the parents of the second generation.

questions.question_text: A spurious association in an ecological study found at population level did not hold at an individual level. What is this called?
questions.explanation: Central limit theorem indicates that, as a sample size increases, the mean approaches a normal distribution. According to the theorem, this is independent of the shape of the distribution. A ceiling effect is an undesirable measurement outcome, occurring when the people on a measurement have reached the maximum possible value. For example, a memory test that assesses how many words a participant can recall has a total of five words that each participant is asked to remember. As most individuals can remember all five words, this measure has a ceiling effect.

questions.question_text: A town in the UK has a population of 90,000. There were 1000 and 1100 patients in 2009 and 2010, respectively, diagnosed with benign melanoma. What was the incidence rate of the disease in 2010 among the town population?
questions.explanation: The incidence rate of the disease is the number of people who develop an illness in a given time period divided by the total number of individuals at risk for the illness during that time period. In the above question, there were 90,000 people in a town. In 2009, there were 1000 people who were diagnosed with melanoma. In 2010, 89,000 people were at risk of developing this condition. The incidence rate in 2010 would be 1100/89,000.

questions.question_text: In the above question what was the prevalence in 2010?
questions.explanation: The prevalence rate is calculated by adding the diagnoses of patient in 2009 (1000) and 2010 (1100) divided by the total population at risk. The prevalence rate in 2010 would be (1000 + 1100)/90,000.

questions.question_text: In a city, the incidence of schizophrenia among people using cannabis was 80/1000 whereas the incidence in those people who did not use cannabis was 20/1000.What is the relative risk of developing schizophrenia in this population?
questions.explanation: The relative risk compares the incidence rate of a disorder among individuals exposed to risk factors, with the incidence rate of the disorder in those who are not exposed. In this example, the chance of developing schizophrenia (relative risk) for the population would be 80/1000 divided by 20/1000 which will be 4. It means that if a person smokes cannabis he is four times at risk of developing schizophrenia than another person who does not use cannabis.

questions.question_text: In the above question what would be the attribution risk?
questions.explanation: The attribution risk helps to determine what would happen in a given population if the risk factor were removed. The attribution risk is calculated by subtracting the incidence rate of people who are exposed to the risk factors (80/1000) from the incidence of those who are not exposed (20/1000).The attribution risk would be 60/1000.

questions.question_text: On the global assessment scale, what is the score for the severe range of symptoms?
questions.explanation: Global assessment of functioning scale is used to measure social, occupational and psychological functioning. The values on the scale range from 0 to 100. The higher the value the better the person's functioning. For example, 0–10 would mean persistent risk to self or others; 21–30 would suggest serious impairment in judgement and almost no ability in functioning; 41–50 suggests serious impairment in functioning in various areas or the person has serious symptoms. The scale can also be used to measure clinical progress in individuals. It is supposed to measure the level of functioning at the time of assessment, i.e. current period.

questions.question_text: Which test is most useful in confirming cerebral dominance before planning destructive brain surgery?

options.text: Repeatable battery for assessment of neuropsychological status

questions.explanation: The Halstead–Reitan neuropsychological battery is used to assess the location of a brain lesion and its effects by 10 tests that measure various neurological functions. It may also help to differentiate depression and early dementia. The Wada test by Juhn Wada (1924) confirms the cerebral dominance in an individual patient, helping to decide on destructive brain surgery. After infusion of amobarbital into the carotid artery of the dominant side, there is step-wise transient aphasia in seconds to minutes. The word association test was developed by Carl Jung; in this the person is given a stimulus word and requested to respond with the 'first' word that comes to his or her mind. Electrophysiological testing is a study of abnormal patterns on standard EEG, which measures and characterises cognitive decline.

questions.question_text: What does an asymmetrical funnel plot indicate?
questions.explanation: A funnel plot works on the assumption that, if all studies conducted about a similar subject were represented graphically by plotting respective effect magnitude against respective sample size, a funnel-shaped distribution would be formed. Publication bias is particularly relevant to systematic reviews. It occurs because studies reporting positive findings are more likely to be accepted for publication in journals than studies that report negative findings.

questions.question_text: Survival times are thought not to obey a normal distribution. Which of the following measures is used?
questions.explanation: Survival probabilities are calculated only when the event of interest occurs in a study. Survival probabilities just before the event are brought forward and adjusted using the post-event survival rate of the remaining uncensored participants. It is this repeated carrying over of survival probabilities that creates a cumulative value, which can be represented pictorially as a Kaplan–Meier survival curve.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is one of the big five personality factors?
questions.explanation: Based on Eysenk's three personality traits, the five big personality factors can be identified over time. Eysenk's three traits are extraversion, neuroticism and psychoticism. The table below provides details of the five big personality traits. Table 4.4 Eysenck's personality traits and big personality factors. Factor Desirable trait Undesirable trait Neuroticism (or emotional stability) Calm, even tempered Anxious, moody, impulsive, temperamental Extraversion Outgoing, social, assertive Introverted, reserved, passive Openness to experience Imaginative, intelligent, creative Shallow, unsophisticated, unperceptive Agreeableness Kind, trusting, warm, altruistic Hostile, selfish, cold Conscientiousness Organised, thorough, tidy, competent Careless, unreliable, sloppy

questions.question_text: Which of the following factors is associated with higher rates of inpatient admissions in patients with borderline personality disorder?
questions.explanation: A pilot study was conducted by Comtois et al (2003) to identify factors associated with high rates of inpatient admission in people with borderline personality disorders. The sample size was 29 and included both Spanish- and English-speaking people. More than half of the sample had high rates of inpatient admission. The results revealed that high levels of admission to wards were associated with a history of parasuicide in the preceding 2 years, the presence of anxiety disorders and poorer cognitive functioning. The high rates were not associated with severity of para suicides, depressive symptoms and psychosis, or substance misuse problems.

questions.question_text: With regard to the cost of treatment for people with borderline personality disorder, which of the following statements is correct?

options.text: Regular hospital treatment for borderline personality disorder is no more expensive than treatment as usual, and shows considerable cost savings after treatment
Specialist full hospital treatment for borderline personality disorder is no more expensive than treatment as usual, and shows considerable cost savings after treatment
Specialist partial hospital treatment for borderline personality disorder is no more expensive than treatment as usual and shows considerable cost savings after treatment
Specialist partial hospital treatment for borderline personality disorder is more expensive than treatment as usual, and shows considerable cost savings after treatment
Specialist partial hospital treatment for borderline personality disorder is no more expensive than treatment as usual, and does not show considerable cost savings after treatment

correct_answer.text: Specialist partial hospital treatment for borderline personality disorder is no more expensive than treatment as usual and shows considerable cost savings after treatment

correct_answers.text: Specialist partial hospital treatment for borderline personality disorder is no more expensive than treatment as usual and shows considerable cost savings after treatment

questions.explanation: Bateman and Fonagy (2003) compared the health care utilisation of patients with borderline personality disorder in a partial hospital treatment setting with treatment as usual. They found that there was no difference in pre- and post-treatment in the two groups. The increased cost of partial hospitalisation was offset by reduced psychiatric inpatient admissions and emergency care. The authors concluded that specialist partial hospital treatment for borderline personality disorder is similar in cost to treatment as usual. Furthermore, it showed a cost saving after the treatment.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is effective in the treatment of schizotypal personality disorder?
questions.explanation: Symptoms of schizotypal personality disorder such as ideas of reference and illusions can be treated with antipsychotic medication. Koenigsberg et al (2003) conducted a randomised controlled study that showed significant benefit of risperidone in patients with schizotypal personality disorder. An antipsychotic can be used together with psychotherapy for treatment of schizotypal disorder. In the presence of comorbid depression, an antidepressant may be beneficial.

questions.question_text: As far as the evidence for psychological therapies in borderline personality disorder is concerned, which of the following statements is correct?

options.text: Cognitive–behavioural therapy should be considered if reducing self-harm is a priority
Convincing evidence from randomised controlled trials shows that the individual psychological therapies are effective
Dialectical behavioural therapy is ineffective in reducing self-harm in women
Evidence base for psychological therapies in the treatment of borderline personality disorder is good
Mentalisation-based therapy with partial hospitalisation is effective in reducing suicide attempts and self-harm

correct_answer.text: Mentalisation-based therapy with partial hospitalisation is effective in reducing suicide attempts and self-harm

correct_answers.text: Mentalisation-based therapy with partial hospitalisation is effective in reducing suicide attempts and self-harm

questions.explanation: There is a relatively poor evidence base for psychological therapies for treating borderline personality disorders. Some studies have shown that therapies such as dialectical behavioural therapy (DBT) and MBT with partial hospitalisation reduce suicide attempts, self-harm, anger, aggression and depressive symptoms. It has been suggested that DBT is effective in reducing self-harm and should be considered for women in whom self-harm is a major problem.

questions.question_text: Which of the following correctly defines one of the needs according to Maslow's hierarchy of needs?
questions.explanation: According to Maslow, there is a hierarchy of needs. The lower-order needs must be satisfied before it is possible to satisfy higher-order needs. Table 4.5 Maslow's hierarchy of needs in descending order. Order Example 1. Self-actualisation Achievement 2. Aesthetic Symmetry, order 3. Cognitive Knowledge, understanding 4. Self-esteem Social acceptance, recognition 5. Belonging/social Group membership, affiliation 6. Safety Security, absence of danger 7. Physical/physiological Hunger, thirst

questions.question_text: Which of the following parenting styles results in children who are happy, capable and successful adults?
questions.explanation: The authoritative parental style tends to result in children being happier, more capable and successful. The authoritative style involves rules and boundaries that are executed in a more democratic way. Parents are willing to listen to their children and are more responsive. With the authoritarian style, parents are stricter about following rules, without an explanation as to why these rules need to be followed. They have high demands and are not responsive to their children. The children, in this case, tend to be obedient and proficient, but are less happy with low self-esteem. Indulgent and neglectful are also parental styles.

questions.question_text: What is the most likely effect on a child whose mother has a history of depression?

options.text: Child can develop depression in later life

correct_answer.text: Child can develop depression in later life

correct_answers.text: Child can develop depression in later life

questions.explanation: Children of postnatally depressed mothers show less behavioural disturbances than those with mothers whose illness evolved via different pathways. Children whose mothers are concurrently depressed show:• poorer cognitive outcomes • more behavioural disturbances • more insecure attachments • more difficult temperaments • greater risk of developing depression later in life.

questions.question_text: With regard to effects of maternal mental illness on infants, which of the following statements is correct?

options.text: Bipolar affective disorder has devastating effects on an infant
Depressed mothers develop better relationships with the infants
If identified and treated early, puerperal psychosis is relatively benign
Manic episodes have a devastating effect on relationships with the infants
Postnatal depressive illness does not cause behavioural disturbances in infants

correct_answer.text: If identified and treated early, puerperal psychosis is relatively benign

correct_answers.text: If identified and treated early, puerperal psychosis is relatively benign

questions.explanation: Puerperal psychosis is the acute onset of psychotic symptoms after childbirth. If not identified and treated, psychotic symptoms can continue for several months with significant deterioration in functioning. However, it can resolve within a few days if adequately treated. Bipolar illness, similar to manic illness, has benign effects on the mother's relationship with the infant. Postnatal depressive illness can have delayed effects and may contribute to late-onset behavioural problems in the infant.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is considered as an explanatory model for mothers acting as an agent for the development of child psychopathology?

options.text: Children of mothers with postnatal depression have no continuing disadvantages
Postnatal depression is more apparent in children coming from deprived backgrounds
Serious consequences for the children do not occur as a result of maternal mental illness

correct_answer.text: Postnatal depression is more apparent in children coming from deprived backgrounds

correct_answers.text: Postnatal depression is more apparent in children coming from deprived backgrounds

questions.explanation: The following are known agents in the explanatory model of how a mother influences the development of child psychopathology: • Maternal mental illness directly provokes child psychopathology, e.g. infanticide in postnatal depression • Maternal mental illness indirectly impairs children via disturbed attachments • Maternal mental illness causes general parenting impediments and therefore in turn impairs attachments • Maternal mental illness distorts child development, e.g.poor cognitive development in children whose mothers were postnatally depressed • Common genetic loading expressed differently at different ages • Mentally ill mothers are less effective at protecting their children from adversity.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is considered an explanatory model for the child to act as an agent in the development of psychopathology in the mother?

options.text: Children having no impact on marital intimacy
Children with difficult temperaments being less likely to have depressed mothers

questions.explanation: The following are known agents in the explanatory model of how a child influences the development of psychopathology in the mother: • Childbirth as an insult • Difficult child temperament in abuse and maternal mental illness • Parenting problems and humiliation from child behaviour contributing to maternal mental illness • Impact of children on marital intimacy • Ill or disabled children.

questions.question_text: Who proposed the strange situation test?
questions.explanation: The strange situation test and adult attachment interview were described by Ainsworth. The strange situation test explores the concepts of attachment proposed by Bowlby. Harlow, through his experiments in monkeys, showed that infants need both warmth and food. Rutter studied the effects of maternal privation and deprivation on children.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements describes the concept of goodness of fit most accurately?

options.text: A child should be easy, active and sociable
Mother does not have to be perfect, but good enough
Negative developments arise in a child when the temperament and environment match
There are reciprocal relations hips between a baby and the environment

correct_answer.text: There are reciprocal relations hips between a baby and the environment

correct_answers.text: There are reciprocal relations hips between a baby and the environment

questions.explanation: Thomas and Chess described the goodness of fit when a reciprocal relationship between a child and its environment, especially with the mother, exists. This is different to the concept of the good-enough mother proposed by Winnicott. The EAS model (Figure 4.1) describes the three-dimensions of temperament such as emotionality, activity and sociability. A difficult temperament in a child may adapt to a harsh environment and help with survival.

questions.question_text: Which of the following concepts was proposed by Bowlby?
questions.explanation: According to Bowlby, inner working models are formed from our early experiences of caregiving, which are carried forward onto new relationships during our lifetime. These working models then affect our perception and behaviour. Bem, a behavioural therapist, devised the self-perception theory. Sigmund Freud devised the theory of motivation. Hobbes devised the theory of hedonism. Tolman described cognitive behaviourism and social learning.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is an important contribution of Carl Jung to the field of psychoanalysis?
questions.explanation: Carl Jung described the unconscious impulses towards a psychic counterpart called an archetype, such as shadow, the self, the anima, the animus and the persona. Melanie Klein was particularly concerned with describing the earliest infantile conflicts and anxieties. Klein's contributions to psychoanalysis include the concept of internal object and the internal world, the primitive mental processes of splitting and projective identification, and the paranoid–schizoid and depressive position.

questions.question_text: Which of the following theories was proposed by Freud?

options.text: Attachment and effects of early experiences

correct_answer.text: Attachment and effects of early experiences

correct_answers.text: Attachment and effects of early experiences

questions.explanation: Freud is known for his contribution with theories on motivation, dreams and the relationship between sleep and dreams, attachment and effects of early experiences, moral and gender development, and aggression. Stephen Jay Gould is known for his theory on evolution of adult consciousness. According to Gould, adult consciousness evolves as the person releases him- or herself from the constraints and ties of childhood consciousness.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about reinforcement is correct?

options.text: Being paid monthly is an example of fixed-ratio reinforcement
Commissioning is a type of continuous reinforcement
Extinction occurs rapidly in variable-interval reinforcement
Gambling is an example of variable-ratio reinforcement
Resistance to extinction is high in continuous reinforcement

correct_answer.text: Gambling is an example of variable-ratio reinforcement

correct_answers.text: Gambling is an example of variable-ratio reinforcement

questions.explanation: Resistance to extinction is very high in variable-interval and variable-ratio reinforcement. In this case, the response is reinforced after an unpredictable number of responses. In continuous reinforcement, resistance to extinction is very low, and every single response is reinforced. Being regularly paid is a type of fixed interval reinforcement, which has a low resistance to extinction. Piecework and commissioning are examples of fixed-ratio reinforcement.

questions.question_text: Which of the following mechanisms takes place in dreams?
questions.explanation: In dreams, the underlying (latent) wishes are converted to manifest content. Displacement happens in dreams in which the real target is substituted by a person or an object that becomes the target of those feelings. In condensation, more than one dream may be 'condensed' into a single manifest image. Concrete representation refers to expression of an abstract idea in a concrete way.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is used in providing an incentive as part of contingency management in patients who misuse drugs?
questions.explanation: Contingency management in patients with drug misuse uses four methods of providing incentives if a patient remains abstinent from the illicit drug. One of the methods is clinic incentive which includes direct benefits from the clinic such as taking methadone home on providing a negative sample. Another method is a voucher-based incentive in which patients receive vouchers with a monetary value. Prize-based incentive includes lottery-style tickets, which have a 50% chance of winning some money. Finally, the patients may also receive direct monies as part of the incentive.

questions.question_text: According to the current evidence, which of the following statements about psychological therapies in drug misuse is correct?

options.text: Contingency management is associated with continuous periods of abstinence in cocaine misuse
Couple-based behavioural therapy is used where both partners are misusing drugs
Relapse prevention has been found to be an effective treatment for cocaine dependence
Relapse prevention has been found to be an effective treatment for heroin dependence
Social systems interventions were developed primarily for elderly people misusing drugs

correct_answer.text: Contingency management is associated with continuous periods of abstinence in cocaine misuse

correct_answers.text: Contingency management is associated with continuous periods of abstinence in cocaine misuse

questions.explanation: When considering psychological therapies for patients with drug misuse, behavioural couples therapy can be considered where the partner is supportive and willing to participate in the therapy. Social systems intervention includes people who are involved in the care of young people such as parents, carers, teachers or friends. Neither relapse-prevention nor standard cognitive behavioural therapy has been found to be effective for the treatment of cocaine dependence. Various studies have shown that, for cocaine misusers, contingency management has been shown to be effective.

questions.question_text: According to the current evidence, which of the following statements about psychological therapies delivered in the outpatient settings for anorexia nervosa is correct?

options.text: Cognitive–behavioural therapy (CBT) is more acceptable to patients than dietary counselling after weight restoration in hospital
One of the aims of therapy is to prevent deliberate self-harm and suicide attempts
There is good evidence that family interventions at tertiary centres are superior to 'treatment as usual'
There is good evidence that family intervention is superior to interpersonal therapy by the end of treatment
There is limited evidence that individual supportive psychotherapy is superior to family therapy in terms of weight gain

correct_answer.text: There is limited evidence that individual supportive psychotherapy is superior to family therapy in terms of weight gain

correct_answers.text: There is limited evidence that individual supportive psychotherapy is superior to family therapy in terms of weight gain

questions.explanation: Psychological therapy in patients with anorexia nervosa is aimed at not only weight gain and healthy eating, but also promoting psychological health. Few studies have compared family interventions and focal psychoanalytic psychotherapy with treatment as usual and have found them effective. There is insufficient evidence in adult populations with regard to any one effective therapy. However, research on weight gain points towards supportive psychological therapy being better than family therapy.

questions.question_text: According to the current evidence, which of the following is an effective psychological therapy for the treatment of anorexia nervosa?
questions.explanation: An effective therapy suggested for patients with anorexia nervosa (AN) is focal psychodynamic psychotherapy. It is a time-limited psychodynamic psychotherapy. Other therapies that have shown benefit in AN patients include cognitive–analytic therapy, cognitive–behavioural therapy (CBT) and interpersonal therapy. For bulimia nervosa, psychological therapies considered include CBT–bulimia nervosa (CBT–BN), CBT with exposure and response prevention, guided self-help and simplified dialectical behaviour therapy.

questions.question_text: According to the current evidence, which of the following statements about psychological therapies in bulimia nervosa is correct?

options.text: Cognitive behavioural therapy–bulimia nervosa (CBT-BN) is more acceptable to patients than interpersonal therapy–bulimia nervosa (IPT-BN), psychodynamic psychotherapy or dietary counselling
CBT-BN is superior to dietary counselling for managing purging by the end of treatment
CBT-BN is superior to dietary counselling for managing purging by the end of follow-up
IPT-BN is superior to CBT-BN in terms of remission from binge eating
IPT-BN is superior to CBT-BN in terms of remission from purging

correct_answer.text: CBT-BN is superior to dietary counselling for managing purging by the end of treatment

correct_answers.text: CBT-BN is superior to dietary counselling for managing purging by the end of treatment

questions.explanation: There is strong evidence that CBT–BN is superior to interpersonal therapybulimia nervosa (IPT-BN) in terms of remission from binge eating and purging. CBT–BN is superior to dietary counselling for managing purging by the end of treatment but not by the end of follow-up. CBT–BN is no more acceptable than other forms of psychotherapy or dietary counselling.

questions.question_text: According to the current evidence, which of the following statements about psychological therapies for treating depression is correct?

options.text: Ten to twelve sessions of CBT are sufficient for most patients to achieve lasting remission
Sixteen to twenty sessions of both psychodynamic psychotherapy and CBT are insufficient for most patients to achieve lasting remission
Sixteen to twenty sessions of psychodynamic psychotherapy are sufficient for most patients to achieve lasting remission
CBT is superior to short-term psychodynamic psychotherapy in improving social functioning
CBT is superior to short-term psychodynamic psychotherapy in treating depressive symptoms

correct_answer.text: Sixteen to twenty sessions of both psychodynamic psychotherapy and CBT are insufficient for most patients to achieve lasting remission

correct_answers.text: Sixteen to twenty sessions of both psychodynamic psychotherapy and CBT are insufficient for most patients to achieve lasting remission

questions.explanation: No significant difference has been found in a meta-analytic study between short-term psychodynamic psychotherapy and CBT on effects of depressive symptoms and social functioning, and in terms of patient remission or improvement. Sixteen to twenty sessions of both therapies were found to be insufficient for most patients to achieve lasting remission.

questions.question_text: According to the current evidence, which of the following statements about delivery of psychological therapies to patients is correct?

options.text: CBT research has focused on the development and mechanism of action rather than evaluating treatment programmes
For more complex interventions, therapists require longer training to be competent therapists
Guided self-help without seeing a skilled therapist in post-traumatic stress disorder has outcomes similar to those when a therapist is available
Self-study-assisted CBT with a few individual sessions is inferior to full CBT
Therapist's personal attributes and styles are more important than therapist training

correct_answer.text: For more complex interventions, therapists require longer training to be competent therapists

correct_answers.text: For more complex interventions, therapists require longer training to be competent therapists

questions.explanation: Therapist training is more important than personal attributes and styles. Some complex therapies require therapists who have trained for longer periods than others. These therapies include trauma-focused CBT and CBT for psychotic illnesses. CBT research has focused on its development rather than its mechanism of action. Studies that have compared styles of CBTs have shown that self-study CBT can be as good as full CBT if given along with a few individual sessions. However, for post-traumatic stress disorder, a skilled therapist is needed for a good outcome.

questions.question_text: According to current evidence, which of the following statements about psychotherapy for patients with depression or dysthymia is correct?

options.text: Sixteen to twenty sessions of psychotherapy are required for the optimal effects of psychotherapy
Combined treatment is better than psychotherapy alone but equal in efficacy compared with pharmacotherapy
Psychotherapy is almost as effective as pharmacotherapy for depressed patients
Psychotherapy is as good as pharmacotherapy for dysthymic patients
Psychotherapy is better than pharmacotherapy for dysthymic patients

correct_answer.text: Sixteen to twenty sessions of psychotherapy are required for the optimal effects of psychotherapy

correct_answers.text: Sixteen to twenty sessions of psychotherapy are required for the optimal effects of psychotherapy

questions.explanation: In a recent meta-analysis, psychotherapy has been found to be less effective than pharmacotherapy, especially selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors, for patients with depression and dysthymia. questions.question_text: Which of the following is considered as the most effective treatment for binge eating disorder?
questions.explanation: A recent randomised control trial compared CBT, behavioural weight loss and a combination of both. The study involved a 12-month follow-up of 15 patients who were randomly assigned to the three groups. The results revealed that CBT was better at reducing binge eating than behavioural weight loss (BWL). However, the BWL method was superior to CBT alone in reducing weight in patients during the trial. It was noted that 51% of the patients with binge eating who were treated with CBT achieved remission. The remission rates were 36–40% for those who had BWL and a sequential CBT and BWL.

CBT was found to be neither inferior nor superior to applied relaxation
No evidence showed that CBT is more effective than psychodynamic therapy
No evidence showed that CBT is effective in short-term management

questions.explanation: On comparison with CBT applied relaxation therapy had similar outcomes in patients with generalised anxiety disorder. Studies have shown that CBT is effective in patients with generalised anxiety disorder compared with waiting. For short-term outcomes, CBT has also been found to be more effective at reducing anxiety and depressive features than psychodynamic psychotherapy.
